Elena / Chris — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of BrightHome priorities (from call):
- Data isolation & auditability: SOC2 / tenant-level logs required
- Predictable latency for user-facing assistants (p95 target ~120ms)
- Clear SLA / escalation path and timely RCAs for Sev1 incidents
- Ability to run failover tests between regions and to validate canary fallback

Competitive set you mentioned: AWS (Bedrock endpoints), Google Vertex AI, and OpenAI. You asked specifically about how different vendors handle incident response, SLA credits, and the format / timing of RCAs — that’s the main focus of the materials I’m attaching.

Proposed next tests (we can run these in a one-week window you prefer):
1) SLA / incident response test: simulated support ticket for degraded p95 and a follow-up on our escalation path to validate response times and interim updates.
2) Failover simulation: short region failover to validate KV cache warm-up and client-side retry behaviour.
3) Throughput + latency benchmark: 50k tokens/day workload profile at expected concurrency to validate latency SLOs and cost delta vs your existing usage.

Attachments: BrightHome-test-plan-v1.pdf (detailed steps), SLA-incident-comparison-matrix.xlsx (vendor timelines & credits), redwood-enterprise-rca-template.pdf (example RCA format).

Immediate asks / owners:
- Elena: confirm which test window (next Tue/Wed?) and whether Chris should run the failover with your infra team.
- Jordan / Monica: can you prepare the vendor incident comparison + a one-page RCA process summary for enterprise customers (I’ve cc’d you).

I’ll also surface how we differ on incident handling vs hyperscalers: short version — proactive fallbacks (model variant + region routing), enterprise SLA with phone escalation for Sev1, and an RCA cadence that includes security/audit artifacts when needed. I’ll include specifics in the matrix.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik / team / Elena — attaching the comparison matrix and the anonymized RCA example per request. High-level points to call out for BrightHome: 

- Initial acknowledgement: Redwood enterprise support (P1/Sev1) — initial ack within 4 hours, phone escalation available within 2 hours of P1 designation.
- Interim updates: standard cadence is every 2 hours for Sev1 until mitigation is in place; we provide a public incident timeline for hosted customers and a private timeline for enterprise with security artefacts if requested.
- Final RCA: target 10 business days for a substantive RCA for Sev1 that includes timeline, root cause, mitigation, and preventative actions. If regulatory artifacts are required (audit logs, packet captures), those are provided as part of the enterprise RCA package within the same window or sooner where permitted.
- Credit calculation: credits are initiated automatically when SLA thresholds are breached; for enterprise customers we can apply credits to monthly invoice or issue a dedicated credit note based on contract preference.

Comparison vs hyperscalers (summary):
- AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex: large providers often have slower personalized interim updates; public postmortems are comprehensive but can be delayed for cross-team incidents. E.g., the Mar 2026 Bedrock region incident’s public postmortem took ~18 days to surface with limited interim cadence for specific customer impacts.
- OpenAI: generally fast public comms but credits and enterprise phone escalation vary and often default to standard support tiers unless an enterprise contract is in place.

Attachments included: SLA-incident-comparison-matrix.xlsx, redwood-enterprise-rca-template.pdf

If BrightHome wants, we can run the SLA response test as a scripted ticket: Redwood will simulate a degraded p95 event, open a P1, and BrightHome will confirm live interim updates and phone escalation.
